errors.text: The cited evidence concerns high-temperature mechanical strength and nanoscale deformation, not yttrium additions, Y2O3 formation, or oxidation resistance in refractory high-entropy alloys.
The hypothesis does not specify the yttrium concentration, incorporation route, exposure duration, thermal cycling, or a quantitative oxidation-rate criterion.
The proposed falsification rule relies on an undefined 'significant improvement,' so it does not provide an unambiguous pass/fail threshold.

It assumes that yttrium will form a continuous protective Y2O3 barrier without evidence; dilute reactive-element additions often modify scale adhesion or transport rather than form the primary continuous oxide scale.
